text:
Joel Farabee is in his second season in Calgary, and so far it's the best scoring stretch of his career: 21 points in 27 games, ten on the power play, and a goal and an assist in the win in Pittsburgh this week.

Our numbers aren't convinced it holds. His scoring rate, 2.43 points per 60, sits above the range we'd expect (roughly 1.6 to 2.3), and the Flames get just 47% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice. His last ten games, five points against nearly eight expected, look closer to the long-run Farabee. The players he resembles most kill penalties, log big minutes, and give up a few chances.

What's real is the role. He's playing over 19 minutes a night, a regular on the power play, and his own chances are up to 1.09 expected goals per 60 from 0.71 last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a transition player: 61% of his shots come off the rush. Watch for him in the first few seconds after a Calgary turnover. Our range has him at 48 to 67 points.
